newsitem.title: USA: Disabled activists back Clinton over Dole.
newsitem.headline: Disabled activists back Clinton over Dole.

text.p: Several activists for the disabled, including a life-long Republican who serves on the Dole Foundation, on Wednesday endorsed President Bill Clinton over Republican Bob Dole, himself disabled by a war injury.

Justin Dart, a moderate Republican on the board of the foundation that Dole founded to help the disabled, said Dole had done his fellow disabled people a disservice by backing House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich's agenda.
"I love the man," Dart said of Dole, whom he had supported for years. "But I love the American dream more ... In 1996 I am a Republican for Clinton."
Wheelchair-bound since 1948 because of polio, Dart worked on disability issues for Republican presidents and helped pay for the wheelchair ramp at the Republicans' headquarters.
But he said the policies now favoured by Republican congressional leaders on health, education, housing, nursing homes and welfare were harmful to disabled people.

Campaign spokeswoman Christina Martin in a statement listed Dole's legislative achievements for the disabled, including his work for passage of the landmark Americans with Disabilities Act in 1990. She said he had also been "an inspiring role model for young people with disabilities."

Dole was badly injured as a young soldier in the Second World War and has permanent damage to his right hand, arm and shoulder. He has difficulty with many simple tasks such as cutting meat on a dinner plate or putting on a coat.
Several of the activists at the news conference have had high profiles in fighting for disability legislation and health reform.
